stories.title: Why early warning signs of glacier collapse in Nepal were difficult to detect
stories.summary: The glacier collapse that led to devastating flash floods across the Himalayan region of Nepal and its border with the Chinese autonomous region of Tibet on August 26 was preceded by early warning signs, experts say. But monitoring and emergency alert systems in the region are still insufficient to predict such disasters.

stories.title: India food safety crackdown targets company of Nepal’s ‘Noodle King’
stories.summary: India ordered CG Foods India, owned by Nepal’s billionaire Binod Chaudhary, to stop some Wai noodle products due to unhygienic practices in their factory. Inspectors found broken noodles collected from the floor were re-processed into bhujia snacks without proper heat treatment, violating food safety rules. Authorities seized 32,000 kg of stock and expired goods, started legal actions, and samples were taken for testing amid a wider food safety crackdown in India. India on Sept 4 ordered a Nepali billionaire’s company popular for its Wai noodles to discontinue some products after an investigation found its factory used unhygienic “floor-collected, broken noodles” in making its Indian snacks. The crackdown is part of an unprecedented food-safety drive in India, where federal and state officials are taking strict action against big and small eateries and brands ranging from Domino’s and Pizza Hut to Diageo for any food safety, hygiene or labelling lapses. The order on Sept 4 was issued to a CG Foods India factory in Rajasthan state in western India, which is part of CG Corp Global, led by Nepal’s only billionaire Binod Chaudhary, nicknamed the “Noodle King”. The regulator’s investigation focused on two Wai-branded products called bhujia – a popular fried Indian snack sold by many companies in the country in tiny packs. Inspectors found “re-processing floor-collected broken noodles into bhujia without heat treatment”, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said in a social media post. In a statement, CG Foods India said it is fully cooperating with the regulatory process and remains “committed to maintaining the highest standards of food safety, quality, and compliance”. Authorities also seized 32,000 kg of stock from the factory, as well as 1,925 boxes of expired finished goods, the FSSAI said, adding that “strict legal proceedings” were initiated against the food business operator. Samples have also been collected for testing, it added.

stories.title: S. Korean won climbs to fresh 14-month high, coupled with strength of Japanese yen
stories.summary: The South Korean won advanced to a fresh 14-month high against the U.S. dollar Friday, correlated with a recent strong gain of the Japanese yen. The won was quoted at 1,350.4 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., up 8.9 won from the close of the previous stock trading session, marking the strongest level since June 30 last year. The won has rebounded in recent weeks as local exporters cut their dollar holdings and SK hynix Inc. converted its proceeds from a mega U.S. listing into the Korean currency. Traders also focused on expectations that Japan's financial authorities may intervene to support the yen, which had suddenly strengthened this week. Foreigners purchased a net 479.3 billion won (US$354 million) worth of local stocks during the latest trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index gaining 1.64 percent to close at 6,687.21.
